purpose: Re-rank Laguna S 2.1 gfx1151 c=1 decode after the gfx1100 transfer, using a same-GGUF Vulkan control, the retained production trace, an active-byte roofline, Qwen3.5 gfx1100-to-gfx1151 lessons, and architecture-local F16 geometry screens.

hardware.read_roof_source: docs/ROOFLINE-gfx1151.md local/reference Mesa RADV+tuned large-read row
hardware.read_roof_qualification: This is the retained same-platform achievable-read anchor, not a fresh HIP counter result from the decode process.

protocol.hipengine_workload: p512/d128 eager c=1; exactly 127 synchronized forward_token calls; BF16 KV; matrix chunk 2048; GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=2
protocol.hipengine_command: GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=2 HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1151 HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE=/tmp/laguna_hipcc_version.txt HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python3 -u scripts/laguna_long_context_profile.py --context-length 4096 --lengths 512 --chunk-size 2048 --decode-output-tokens 128 --repetitions 3 --warmup-rows 128 --compiler-version-file /tmp/laguna_hipcc_version.txt --require-cached-build --output /tmp/laguna-p512-d128-d9-production.json
protocol.vulkan_perf_logger_command: GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER=1 GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER_FREQUENCY=8 /home/lhl/llama.cpp/llama.cpp-vulkan/build/bin/llama-bench -m /home/lhl/models/gguf/laguna-s-2.1-Q4_K_M.gguf -p 0 -n 8 -d 512 -r 1 --no-warmup -o json -fa on -b 2048 -ub 512 -ctk f16 -ctv f16 -ngl -1 -dev Vulkan0 --progress
protocol.comparator_qualification: Same GGUF, GPU, nominal depth, FlashAttention, batch and ubatch. Vulkan uses F16 KV and llama-bench random tokens; hipEngine uses BF16 KV and its deterministic natural trajectory. The row is a directional implementation comparator, not a bit-exact backend race.

active_encoded_weight_bytes_proxy.method: Count every dense/router/output tensor once, 10/256 of each rank-3 expert tensor, and one embedding row. Resident bytes reflect the physical hipEngine decode layout; source bytes reflect the raw GGUF layout.
active_encoded_weight_bytes_proxy.caveat: This is an encoded payload proxy, not a DRAM counter. It excludes activation, KV, metadata and output traffic; cache reuse and selected-expert address variation can move physical traffic.

roofline.interpretation: The whole-model proxy says Vulkan is already close to the practical streaming envelope while hipEngine is not. Family attribution is required because attention is not represented by the weight-byte ledger and cache effects make the proxy non-additive.

hipengine_trace.queue_interpretation: The trace is fully serialized: interval union equals kernel sum. Submission/launch cleanup is bounded to a few percent and cannot explain the Vulkan gap.

vulkan_perf_logger.qualification: The logger perturbs wall and reports graph operation/kernel-family aggregates. Use family ratios, not its 22.13 tok/s row, as the comparator decomposition.
source_findings: n=1 routes through Vulkan one-row MMV/MMV-ID rather than the prefill MMQ path; mul_mat_vec_max_cols is 8.
On AMD, Q4_K with K>=2048 can quantize the activation to reusable Q8_1 and use integer dot; Q6_K is explicitly excluded from MMVQ and stays on the floating dequant path.
The AMD decode kernels use subgroup-oriented one-row ownership; RADV STRIX_HALO reports subgroup64.
FlashAttention fuses the 48 D128 GQA layers instead of materializing hipEngine's score plane and replaying a scalar slot-order value reducer.

gap_attribution.interpretation: Attention is the first architecture task. F16 remains second. Selected expert kernels are already close enough to the practical read roof that another generic Qwen quant port is lower leverage.

attention_kv_payload_at_live512.interpretation: The current split score producer is cheap; 86.1% of attention time is in the global/SWA reducers. A useful replacement must parallelize K and reuse each KV head across its six global or nine SWA query heads without collapsing the grid below gfx1151 occupancy.

architecture_local_f16_geometry_screens.method: One cached full-model p512/d128 run per candidate. Only rows==1 F16 single/triple launches were monkeypatched to the requested legal thread count; prefill remained local256. Candidate code was not retained.
architecture_local_f16_geometry_screens.decision: Reject simple local64/local128 substitution before quality work. Retain local256. The next F16 premise is an exact eight-wave/eight-output block where each wave reconstructs the current eight partial sequences for one output and avoids cross-wave barriers; it is not another thread-count sweep.

qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.lesson: Transfer ownership and reuse hypotheses, not fixed bodies or thresholds.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.qwen_evidence: gfx1151 needed native C2/C4/C8 execution, a 5+3 LM-head partition instead of gfx1100 6+2, and C8-only pair reuse.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.laguna_application: Use separate D128 qgroup6 global and qgroup9 SWA specializations and tune split count/local size on 40 CUs.

qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.lesson: Physical width is an independent seam.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.qwen_evidence: Several pair-reuse wins promoted only at physical C8 and were neutral or worse at C1/C2/C4.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.laguna_application: This campaign is C1 latency. Do not import C8 pair-reuse conclusions; batch/server throughput keeps separate gates.

qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.lesson: Reduction width is a numerical contract.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.qwen_evidence: gfx1151 admitted whole-row C4/C8 attention because generic row-chunk2 changed row-local numerics.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.laguna_application: Gate global/SWA split-K merge order at live 65/127/257/512, page boundaries, ring wrap and eviction; exact and quality-gated lanes remain separate.

qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.lesson: Preserve grid breadth on the 40-CU target.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.qwen_evidence: Target-specific occupancy widths won while broad workgroup collapses failed; Laguna's own qhead3/GQA3 screens lost when 72 workgroups became 24.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.laguna_application: Grouped-GQA attention must create 40-80 or more independent blocks per layer through K64/K128 splits rather than one block per KV head.

qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.lesson: Microkernel wins do not imply cycle wins.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.qwen_evidence: Q8T16 local geometry and pair reuse often shrank a leaf but disappeared or reversed in p512/d128 or serving gates.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.laguna_application: Require actual-weight leaf, full p512/d128, p128/p512/p1K/p4K context seams, full state, lifecycle and heldout quality before promotion.

qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.lesson: Stable ownership is separate from ephemeral execution rows.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.qwen_evidence: Occupancy-adaptive dense rows preserved scheduler, GDN and KV ownership while changing only execution width.
qwen35_gfx1100_to_gfx1151_lessons.laguna_application: Every attention candidate consumes the full KVLiveSpans ABI and preserves page/ring ownership; Laguna has no GDN state to port.

ranked_next_work.title: D128 grouped-GQA split-K decode attention
ranked_next_work.premise: Adapt the Qwen grouped-GQA split-K topology, not its D256/qgroup8 constants. Use separate qgroup6 global and qgroup9 SWA bodies, K64/K128 splits to retain gfx1151 grid breadth, fused score/softmax/PV, and a bounded merge+gate.
ranked_next_work.first_gate: Attention <=3.0 ms/token at p512 with every exact boundary fixture passing; stretch <=1.5 ms/token. Full decode must improve in both process orders before category work.
ranked_next_work.expected_system_ceiling: Recovering 10-13 ms/token moves the current 68.70 ms wall into roughly the 17-18 tok/s range before F16 work.

ranked_next_work.title: Exact F16 wave-owned multi-output GEMV
ranked_next_work.premise: One local256 block owns eight output columns; each wave owns one output and keeps eight per-lane partial sequences so the current 256-thread reduction tree can be reconstructed without LDS or cross-wave barriers.
ranked_next_work.closed_variants: Simple local64 and local128 substitutions are rejected at -4.81% and -2.01%.
ranked_next_work.first_gate: Actual QKV/O shapes must reduce the 30.98 ms family toward the 25.37 ms unchanged-byte floor with bit-exact outputs and no p512/d128 regression.

ranked_next_work.title: Decode-only compressed representation for source-F16 projections
ranked_next_work.premise: Source-F16 owns 61.12% of active resident bytes. A persistent Q8-class decode side representation could remove about 2.8 GB of traffic/token, but adds capacity and a new quality surface.
ranked_next_work.first_gate: Projection-input capture, primitive error/KL screen, complete heldout KL <=0.05 and top-1 >=90%, then context/capacity and p512/d128.

ranked_next_work.title: Dense/shared raw-layout decode and residual quant cleanup
ranked_next_work.premise: Pack8 expands shared/dense Q4 resident traffic and the remaining family is slower than Vulkan, but the complete ceiling is only a few milliseconds.
ranked_next_work.first_gate: Counter or actual-byte evidence plus a complete-wall win; do not reopen selected expert bodies already at about 91% of the read roof.

ranked_next_work.title: Submission replay and residual fusion
ranked_next_work.premise: Current unprofiled wall minus device sum is only about 2.18 ms/token. Graph/AQL work is bounded cleanup after the two dominant kernels.
ranked_next_work.first_gate: A measured repeated submission/synchronization boundary; no launch-count-only promotion.

definition_of_next_pause.near_term_target: >=18 tok/s p512/d128 with the same state and quality contract
definition_of_next_pause.correctness: Kernel CPU-reference gate plus full hidden/logit/KVLiveSpans/reset/lifecycle state; any changed association additionally requires the heldout category KL/top-1 gate.
definition_of_next_pause.stop_rule: Do not resume generic Q4/Q6 selected-expert tuning or launch shaving while attention and F16 explain 77% of the comparator gap.
